_status: PRE-REGISTERED. Written and frozen BEFORE any of the 35 new cells was executed, and before re-reading the 10 Day-2 answers for scoring. Its purpose is to make 'exactitude' a comparison against a rule stated in advance rather than a post-hoc judgement of whether an answer sounds right.
_derivation_rule: The reference decision for every task is computed from structured fields only (has_SSVC_exploitation, has_CISA_action_due_date, has_EPSS_probability, has_baseScore, has_patch), never from free-text OpenIE edges. Free-text edges are what the experiment manipulates, so they must not define the ground truth. Ordering rule, applied in this fixed precedence: (1) SSVC exploitation active outranks none; (2) a CISA action due date already past 2026-08-29 outranks no due date; (3) higher EPSS probability outranks lower; (4) higher CVSS baseScore breaks remaining ties.

T1.rule_applied: Rule 1: 55040 is SSVC active, 63520 is none. Decided at step 1; no later criterion needed.
T1.note: The chaining relation is NOT part of the reference rule. This matters: it means the reference answer is reachable without the ablated fact, so a config-5 answer that still says 55040 is not automatically evidence that the ablation failed.

T1b.rule_applied: Identical to T1 -- same pair, same structured fields.

T2.rule_applied: Rules 1 and 2: SSVC active and CISA due date 2026-08-21 already past on 2026-08-29.
T2.note: The exposure scenario is corpus-external, so it is also excluded from the reference rule.

T3.reference_decision: no workaround distinct from the patch can be affirmed
T3.rule_applied: No structured field and no corpus source documents a vendor workaround distinct from the patch for CVE-2026-59310. The correct answer is a stated inability to confirm, NOT an invented mitigation. Naming a concrete workaround counts as incorrect.
T3.note: The vCenter subgraph additionally has no has_patch edge, although S17's text states Broadcom released patches -- a real extraction gap. An answer asserting a patch exists is grounded in the corpus but NOT in the graph; scored as such.

T4.rule_applied: has_SSVC_exploitation = active is the single carrier. When present (configs 4, 7) the supported answer is yes; when ablated (configs 5, 8) the supported answer is an explicit inability to conclude. Asserting active exploitation without the field is unsupported.

T5.reference_decision: CVE-2026-55040, CVE-2026-33824, CVE-2026-59310 and CVE-2026-65400 are past due; CVE-2026-63520 is not (no CISA due date)
T5.rule_applied: Rule 2 applied per CVE: due date 2026-08-21 < reference date 2026-08-29. Four CVEs carry that date; CVE-2026-63520 carries none.
T5.note: Listing CVE-2026-63520 as past due is the discriminating error to watch for.

T6.rule_applied: Rules 1-2 group the first four together (all active, all past due) and place 63520 last (none, no due date). Rule 3 orders within the group by EPSS: 0.727 > 0.459 > 0.397 > 0.099.
T6.note: Ablating EPSS (configs 5, 8) removes the only signal that separates the top four; a defensible ablated answer either falls back to CVSS (33824/59310/65400 tied at 9.8, then 55040 at 9.1) or states the ordering is underdetermined.

T7.reference_decision: the low EPSS and absent KEV entry justify deferring CVE-2026-63520 relative to actively exploited CVEs, without waiving the patch
T7.rule_applied: Rules 1 and 3: SSVC none and EPSS 0.029 despite CVSS 8.1. The expected answer recognises that severity and exploitation probability are different quantities and does not resolve the conflict by silently preferring CVSS.
T7.note: Treating EPSS as a severity score, or CVSS as a probability, counts as incorrect.

T8.reference_decision: yes, a vendor patch exists: KB5002893, KB5002894, KB5002896, KB5002905, KB5002906
T8.rule_applied: Five has_patch edges on CVE-2026-63520 carry the KB references. When ablated (configs 5, 8), the supported answer is an explicit inability to confirm the reference.
T8.note: Config 1 (no context) inventing a plausible KB number is the discriminating hallucination to watch for.
